arxiv-2101-10655.description: Abstract Recognizing user location with WiFi fingerprints is a popular approach for accurate indoor positioning problems. In this work, our goal is to interpret WiFi fingerprints into actual user locations. However, WiFi fingerprint data can be very high dimensional in some cases, we need to find a good representation of the input data for the learning task first.

arxiv-2111-07753.title: An Adaptive Framework for Reliable Trajectory Following in Changing-Contact Robot Manipulation Tasks
arxiv-2111-07753.creator: Saif Sidhik \affilnum 1, Mohan Sridharan \affilnum 1 and Dirk Ruiken \affilnum 2
arxiv-2111-07753.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Saif Sidhik \affilnum 1, Mohan Sridharan \affilnum 1 and Dirk Ruiken \affilnum 2. We describe a framework for changing-contact robot manipulation tasks that require the robot to make and break contacts with objects and surfaces. The discontinuous interaction dynamics of such tasks make it difficult to construct and use a single dynamics model or control strategy, and the highly non-linear nature of the dynamics during contact changes can be damaging to the robot and the objects.

arxiv-2209-04235.title: IEEE 802.11ad Based Joint Radar Communication Transceiver: Design, Prototype and Performance Analysis
arxiv-2209-04235.creator: Akanksha Sneh, Soumya Jain, V Sri Sindhu, Shobha Sundar Ram, Sumit Darak
arxiv-2209-04235.description: Abstract Rapid beam alignment is required to support high gain millimeter wave (mmW) communication links between a base station (BS) and mobile users (MU). The standard IEEE 802.11ad protocol enables beam alignment at the BS and MU through a lengthy beam training procedure accomplished through additional packet overhead. However, this results in reduced latency and throughput.

arxiv-2303-11313.title: CLIP goes 3D: Leveraging Prompt Tuning for Language Grounded 3D Recognition
arxiv-2303-11313.creator: Deepti Hegde, Jeya Maria Jose Valanarasu, Vishal M. PatelJohns Hopkins University dhegde1,jvalana1,vpatel36@jhu.edu
arxiv-2303-11313.description: Abstract Vision-Language models like CLIP have been widely adopted for various tasks due to their impressive zero-shot capabilities. However, CLIP is not suitable for extracting 3D geometric features as it was trained on only images and text by natural language supervision.

arxiv-2310-10718.title: Inferring fundamental spacetime symmetries with gravitational-wave memory: from LISA to the Einstein Telescope
arxiv-2310-10718.creator: Boris Goncharov, Laura Donnay, Jan Harms
arxiv-2310-10718.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Boris Goncharov, Laura Donnay, Jan Harms. We revisit gravitational wave (GW) memory as the key to measuring spacetime symmetries, extending beyond its traditional role in GW searches. In particular, we show how these symmetries may be probed via displacement and spin memory observations, respectively. We further find that the Einstein Telescope’s (ET) sensitivity enables constraining the strain amplitude of a displacement memory to 2% and that of spin memory to 22%.

arxiv-2310-16363.title: Finite-Time Analysis of Three-Timescale Constrained Actor-Critic and Constrained Natural Actor-Critic Algorithms
arxiv-2310-16363.creator: Prashansa Panda, Shalabh Bhatnagar
arxiv-2310-16363.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Prashansa Panda, Shalabh Bhatnagar. Actor Critic methods have found immense applications on a wide range of Reinforcement Learning tasks especially when the state-action space is large. In this paper, we consider actor critic and natural actor critic algorithms with function approximation for constrained Markov decision processes (C-MDP) involving inequality constraints and carry out a non-asymptotic analysis for both of these algorithms in a non-i.i.d (Markovian) setting.

arxiv-2407-02978.title: Mast Kalandar at SemEval-2024 Task 8: On the Trail of Textual Origins: RoBERTa-BiLSTM Approach to Detect AI-Generated Text
arxiv-2407-02978.creator: Jainit Sushil Bafna, Hardik Mittal, Suyash Sethia, Manish Shrivastava, Radhika Mamidi
arxiv-2407-02978.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jainit Sushil Bafna, Hardik Mittal, Suyash Sethia, Manish Shrivastava, Radhika Mamidi. Large Language Models (LLMs) have showcased impressive abilities in generating fluent responses to diverse user queries. However, concerns regarding the potential misuse of such texts in journalism, educational, and academic contexts have surfaced. SemEval 2024 introduces the task of Multigenerator, Multidomain, and Multilingual Black-Box Machine-Generated Text Detection, aiming to develop automated systems for identifying machine-generated text and detecting potential misuse.

arxiv-2408-14390.title: Spoken-Term Discovery using Discrete Speech Units
arxiv-2408-14390.creator: Benjamin van Niekerk, Julian Zaïdi, Marc-André Carbonneau, Herman Kamper
arxiv-2408-14390.description: Abstract Discovering a lexicon from unlabeled audio is a longstanding challenge for zero-resource speech processing. One approach is to search for frequently occurring patterns in speech. We revisit this idea with DUSTED: Discrete Unit Spoken-TErm Discovery 1 1 1 Code available at https://github.com/bshall/dusted . Leveraging self-supervised models, we encode input audio into sequences of discrete units.

arxiv-2512-12352.title: Modeling the Happiness-Sustainability Nexus via Graphical Lasso and Quantile-on-Quantile Regression
arxiv-2512-12352.creator: Mohamed Chaouch, Thanasis Stengos
arxiv-2512-12352.description: Abstract . This paper investigates the nexus between subjective well-being and sustainability, proxied by the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) Index, using cross-country data from 126 nations in 2022. While prior research has highlighted a positive association between happiness and sustainable development, existing approaches largely rely on linear regressions or correlation-based measures that mask distributional heterogeneity, multicollinearity, and potential nonlinear dependence.

How HIV-1 RT regulates nucleotide selectivity is a central issue for genetics and the nucleoside analog RT inhibitor (NRTI) resistance of H

pmc-10573013.title: Unravelling Heavy Metal Dynamics in Soil and Honey: A Case Study from Maramureș Region, Romania
pmc-10573013.creator: Florin Dumitru Bora, Anca Cristina Babeș, Anamaria Călugăr, Mugurel Ioan Jitea, Adela Hoble, Răzvan Vasile Filimon, Andrea Bunea, Alexandru Nicolescu, Claudiu Ioan Bunea, Carmen Rubio, Jesus Olivero-Verbel, Dirk W Lachenmeier
pmc-10573013.description: The study examined soil and honey samples from the Maramureș region, assessing potentially toxic elements and their concentrations. The highest concentrations were found for (Cu), (Zn), (Pb), (Cr), (Ni), (Cd), (Co), and (As), while (Hg) remained below the detection limit. Samples near anthropogenic sources displayed elevated metal levels, with the Aurul settling pond and Herja mine being major contamination sources.

pmc-11427829.title: Proton Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy for Liver Metastases From Malignant Pancreatic Insulinoma
pmc-11427829.creator: Jake A Kloeber, Daniel K Ebner, Krishan R Jethwa, Kenneth W Merrell, Thorvardur R Halfdanarson, Cameron M Callaghan
pmc-11427829.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Insulin-producing pancreatic tumors are a common subtype of neuroendocrine tumor. Standard of care includes surgical resection of the pancreatic tumor and medical management with somatostatin analogs. For patients with metastatic disease, tumor control and hypoglycemic symptom relief can be achieved through surgical resection of the tumor, hepatic artery embolization, radiofrequency ablation, or radioembolization using radioactive isotopes as well as with systemic therapy such as somatostatin analogs and everolimus. We present the case of a 74-year-old male with metastatic insulin-producing pancreatic carcinoma.

pmc-11516123.title: Closing the gap: introducing the EQUALS MAP framework for equity-focused evidence synthesis
pmc-11516123.creator: L McCann, L Johnson, A Gkiouleka, H Pearce, J Ford
pmc-11516123.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundEquity-focused analysis is vital to understanding how interventions affect disadvantaged groups and prevent widening inequalities via intervention-generated inequalities. We reviewed PROGRESS-Plus usage - a commonly used framework in equity-focused reviews and proposed a novel framework.MethodsFirst, we re-analysed articles from the EQUALISE study, a review of interventions that increase or decrease inequalities in general practice, to explore the various domains of disadvantage examined in the included studies. We then compared these domains of disadvantage with the existing PROGRESS-Plus framework.

pmc-12554144.title: Targeting ER stress-mediated apoptosis by MSC-derived exosomes: A novel therapeutic strategy against pulmonary fibrosis
pmc-12554144.creator: Ruixi Luo, Yaqiong Wei, La Wang, Peng Chen, Didong Lou, Weiyi Tian
pmc-12554144.description: IntroductionIdiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is marked by a gradual decline in pulmonary function over time and is associated with a grim prognosis. In the pathogenesis of IPF, persistent endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress plays a significant role in promoting fibrosis through pathways involving apoptosis. Mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (MSC-Ex) have shown promise in mitigating pulmonary fibrosis by inhibiting apoptosis.

pmc-12655458.title: Computational Chemistry Advances in the Development of PARP1 Inhibitors for Breast Cancer Therapy
pmc-12655458.creator: Charmy Twala, Penny Govender, Krishna Govender, Giulia Culletta, Marco Tutone
pmc-12655458.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase 1 (PARP1) is an important enzyme that plays a central role in the DNA damage response, facilitating repair of single-stranded DNA breaks via the base excision repair (BER) pathway and thus genomic integrity. Its therapeutic relevance is compounded in breast cancer, particularly in BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutant cancers, where compromised homologous recombination repair (HRR) leaves a synthetic lethal dependency on PARP1-mediated repair.

pmc-12991367.title: RND-mediated efflux couples antimicrobial resistance and hypervirulence in contemporary Vibrio cholerae
pmc-12991367.creator: Yuding Weng, X. Renee Bina, Mia E. Van Allen, James E. Bina
pmc-12991367.description: The prevailing view in bacterial pathogenesis is that antimicrobial resistance and virulence are constrained by evolutionary trade-offs, with resistance mechanisms imposing fitness costs that attenuate pathogenic potential. Herein we document that contemporary Vibrio cholerae clinical isolates from the ongoing seventh pandemic have circumvented this paradigm by coupling multidrug resistance with hypervirulence.

pmc-13156701.title: A Cell-Based Protocol to Assess Manganese Content and Relative Transport Activity of Manganese Transporters
pmc-13156701.creator: Huiwei Zhong, Xurui Shen, Hanting Yang
pmc-13156701.description: Manganese (Mn) is an essential trace element whose intracellular homeostasis is tightly controlled by specialized membrane transporters. Dysregulation of Mn transport leads to pathological Mn accumulation and severe human disease; however, efficient and quantitative cell-based methods for assessing Mn2+ transporter activity remain limited.

pmc-13159128.title: Rapid Proteome‐Wide Discovery of Protein–Protein Interactions With ppIRIS
pmc-13159128.creator: Luiz Felipe Piochi, Di Tang, Johan Malmström, Yasaman Karami, Hamed Khakzad
pmc-13159128.description: Protein–protein interactions (PPIs) are central to cellular processes and host‐pathogen dynamics across all domains of life, yet comprehensive interactome mapping remains challenging at the proteome scale. Experimental approaches provide only partial coverage, while existing computational methods often lack generalizability across species or are too resource‐intensive for large‐scale screening.

pmc-13284927.title: Building a Gateway for Prison Re-Entry: An Interview with Change Agent Philip Cooper
pmc-13284927.creator: Philip Cooper
pmc-13284927.description: In this interview, Operation Gateway Chief Change Agent Philip Cooper discusses his organization, working to reduce the stigma of recovery and re-entry, and various policies impacting community-based organizations’ ability decrease prison recidivism. Introduction In Western North Carolina, Operation Gateway’s staff are “change agents” working every day to help people manage the transition from incarceration back into society.

pmc-13503277.title: Data for famine and extreme emergencies: challenges and opportunities
pmc-13503277.creator: Daniel Maxwell, Peter Hailey, Elena Naumova
pmc-13503277.description: High-quality data are a pre-requisite for the development of models—whether of famine or food and nutrition-related emergencies. We highlighted challenges, related to data in famines or near-famine emergencies, including data availability, quality, timeliness, and sharing; the misuse of data could be a real threat for applying new advanced data analytic tools, such as artificial intelligence and machine learning.
